clue.text: Not much of a difference for coppers

blocks.note: first meaning: a minor alteration that hardly matters
second meaning: low-value coins, which in Britain are copper-coloured pennies

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that a change of policy will make little difference to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police officers, but here it means the copper coins (1p and 2p pieces) in a British pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a trivial adjustment and loose coins of low value, the second being its literal sense.

clue.text: Wash second baby

blocks.note: mo is a short moment, informally a second
a pup is a baby animal, such as a young dog or seal

explanation.surface: A parent bathes their younger child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second baby' reads as a younger sibling, but second is a unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up spilled liquid with a cloth or mop is a form of washing a surface.

clue.text: Express didn’t have crew, they said

indicators.note: what people said is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: a rowing crew is an eight, so to be without one is to have lacked eight

explanation.surface: A train service was reportedly short of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' suggests a train, but it is the verb for squeezing out milk.
explanation.definitionFit: To express milk is to draw it from the breast, and producing or secreting milk is what lactating means.

clue.text: Height 110 around capital city

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the number's letters enclose the city

blocks.note: 110 in Roman numerals is C (100) plus X (10)
Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: Something reaches 110 metres around a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A climax is the peak or highest point of something, as height can mean the culmination or summit.

clue.text: Tail of ruminant grabbed by a smarter animal

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, so only that is kept
what is grabbed is held inside the grasp of the words that follow

blocks.note: a + neater, smarter in the sense of tidier
the last letter of ruminant

explanation.surface: A cleverer beast seizes the tail of a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smarter' reads as cleverer, but it means neater, as in smartly dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The anteater is a long-snouted South American mammal that feeds on termites and ants, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Brutal force goes wrong: light touch accepted

indicators.note: going wrong means getting out of order, so these letters get jumbled
something accepted is taken in, so it goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a tap is a gentle touch

explanation.surface: A heavy-handed police operation goes awry, when a gentler approach is welcomed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany, notorious for its cruelty.

clue.text: Modern nation frequently requiring compassion

blocks.note: a state is a nation
oft is an old word for often
to have heart is to show compassion

explanation.surface: A contemporary country often calls for kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the most advanced, up-to-date level of technology or design, so it means up to the minute.

clue.text: Dessert I stuff inside suit, messily

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so these letters are put in the other word
something done messily is untidy, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A guest stuffs a pudding inside their suit and makes a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian pudding of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone, an example of a sweet course.

clue.text: Rural county: cars let out south of this place

indicators.note: in a down entry, south of means placed below, so these pieces come after

blocks.note: here means this place
Fords are cars made by the Ford company
to hire out is to let something out for payment

explanation.surface: In a country district, cars are rented out south of here.
explanation.walkthrough: HEREFORDSHIRE is a largely agricultural English county on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English county known for farmland, cider orchards and cattle, so a rural one.

clue.text: Subject for choosing, finally forgotten

indicators.note: the end of the phrase is forgotten, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: 'for choosing' read as the phrase 'to pick'

explanation.surface: A subject is put forward to be chosen, with the last item left out.
explanation.walkthrough: TO PICK loses its final K to give TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter under discussion, a direct synonym for a subject.

clue.text: Food processor undergoing trial in back of cafe

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: something undergoing a trial is 'in test'
taken as written
the last letter of cafe

explanation.surface: A new kitchen blender is being tested out at the rear of a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food processor' sounds like a kitchen gadget, but it is the body's own processor of food.
explanation.definitionFit: The gut is where eaten material is digested and absorbed, so it literally processes what we eat.

clue.text: Boss, best of the bunch?

blocks.note: first meaning: informal term for the person in charge
second meaning, playful: the finest fruit in a bunch of bananas

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second reading is taken literally, as a bunch of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is slang for the leader or most important person, and literally suggests the uppermost fruit on a stalk.

clue.text: Shock in a puzzle

blocks.note: taken as written
a maze is a puzzle of winding paths

explanation.surface: Someone is left dazed while stuck in a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or stun someone is a verb meaning much the same as to startle them.

clue.text: Large number rarely cut, zero sent back

indicators.note: a word that is cut is trimmed, losing its final letter
sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: a synonym for rarely
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A big figure is seldom trimmed, and nothing is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: SELDOM loses its M, takes O, and the whole SELDOO is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal plural noun for lots or heaps of something, a plentiful quantity.

clue.text: Saucy thing, part of morning routine

blocks.note: first meaning: a sauce poured over salad
second meaning: putting on clothes after getting up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' hints at something cheeky, but here it literally means sauce-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a salad sauce such as vinaigrette and the act of putting on clothes each day.

clue.text: Weirdly porcine, old cheese from sheep

indicators.note: doing something weirdly means doing it in an odd way, so these letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An aged ewe's-milk cheese strangely resembles something piggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porcine' means pig-like, a joke against the sheep the cheese actually comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Pecorino is an Italian hard cheese made from ewe's milk; the name comes from pecora, Italian for a ewe.

clue.text: Twist isn’t cosmetic

blocks.note: to warp is to twist out of shape
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone insists a twisted thing is not merely superficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, war paint is make-up, a jokey name for face products worn like tribal markings.

clue.text: Article pains ham actor

indicators.note: to ham is to overact clumsily, so the word next to it is badly performed and jumbled

blocks.note: the definite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper article hurts an actor known for overacting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham actor' reads as one phrase, but 'ham' is the anagram signal and 'actor' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a formal or jokey term for a performer on stage, after Thespis of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Nerve required to climb over brave person in passenger seat

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
in a down entry, over means placed above, so this part comes first

blocks.note: lip is cheek or impudent nerve
a lion is a type for a courageous person

explanation.surface: Someone needs courage to clamber over a hero sitting as a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillion is the rear seat on a motorcycle where a rider's passenger sits.

clue.text: Flourish with a leap

blocks.note: taken as written
a bound is a leap or jump

explanation.surface: Someone shows off with a theatrical jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' looks like a showy gesture to go with the leap, but it is the verb meaning thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plentiful or thrive in large numbers is a meaning shared by both verbs.

clue.text: Islanders: unknown number in bistro, drunk

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it
someone drunk staggers about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: n is the algebraic symbol for an unknown number
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tipsy people from an island are drinking in a small restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons live on Great Britain, an island, so they are islanders in the literal sense.

clue.text: Heavy weight carried by wizard immediately

indicators.note: what is carried is held within the carrier, so it goes inside

blocks.note: an ace or wizard is an expert
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: A magician lifts a huge load in an instant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' suggests a magician, but it means someone brilliant at something.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverbial phrase means without delay, right now, so it is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: A supporter of the arts?

blocks.note: surface reading: a patron who funds galleries and theatres
setter's reading: a wooden stand that literally holds up a painting while it is made

explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a benefactor; the question mark warns it is a physical prop for canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's three-legged frame physically bears the weight of a canvas, so it supports art in the literal sense.

clue.text: Father dead-headed rose in garden plot

indicators.note: deadheading a plant removes its spent top, so the first letter goes
one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a briar is a wild rose
a small piece of ground for growing things

explanation.surface: A gardener's dad deadheads a rose growing in the vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' wants to be a flower name like CAMELLIA; it is the wild rose of hedgerows, and deadheading here removes just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family, a dignified word for a paternal figure.

clue.text: Domain: actual kingdom, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word before is kept

blocks.note: real means actual
the last letter of kingdom

explanation.surface: A territory turns out to be a genuine kingdom in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kingdom' tempts as the definition, but it only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a territory or sphere of influence, so a field or area one rules over.

clue.text: Move tried on in performance

indicators.note: the instruction to move tells us to shift these letters into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dance step is rehearsed during a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a particular interpretation or rendering of a song or piece, so a performance of it.

clue.text: Broadcasting in Bulgarian, old revolutionary

indicators.note: the letters sit in the words that follow, spanning them
a revolution turns things round, so the found letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the tail of Bulgarian plus the start of old

explanation.surface: A transmission is going out in Bulgarian about an aged rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old revolutionary' looks like a veteran rebel; the letters RIANO hide across the comma and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme being transmitted live is said to be going out over the airwaves, the idiom for broadcasting.

clue.text: Ridiculously hot man, dense to put it mildly

indicators.note: something done ridiculously is absurd and disordered, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gorgeous man is also rather thick, and that's an understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom adds emphasis meaning 'and more besides', admitting an earlier statement understated things.
